newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares end up a hair despite strike worry.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares end up a hair despite strike worry.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed fractionally higher in slow trade with investors cautious about taking positions ahead of Wednesday's 12-hour national work stoppage, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 0.49 percent to 9,284.62, as 25 stocks rose, 14 fell and three closed flat.
"Although there is uncertainty about tomorrow's strike, the market is resisting falls because it is assumed that the strike will go off quietly," InverUnion broker Hector Perez said.
Volume was thin with 906 trades for 4.028 billion bolivars ($8.1 million).
Brokers said that few investors were selling positions and many more were waiting to re-enter the market once the labor dispute had passed.

Among leading benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 6.00 bolivars to 810.00 bolivars, telephone company CANTV rose 40.00 bolivars to 3,045.00 bolivars and steel company Sivensa slipped 0.75 bolivars to 267.75 bolivars.
